messages:
sara (eng-platform): Heads-up: console team started showing per-route "quota bands" (low/med/high burn) but our ingestion currently keys off the legacy header. If we flip the client header in the upcoming SDK change it will break attribution in the dashboard.
kevin (devex): which header exactly?
linh (eng): new SDK PR renames the wire header to `X-RW-Policy` (from `X-Redwood-Policy`) to match API contract simplification. It's a small proto rename in clients.
dmitri (eng-runtime): Server can accept both headers, but our telemetry pipeline normalizes keys during ingestion. We need to map the new header to the existing canonical route id so the heatmaps don't go blank.
kevin (devex): I want the SDK change (TS + Py) but without causing a sudden console gap. Options: 1) dual-accept server-side for 2 weeks; 2) SDK sends both headers for one release; 3) console maps by token+route fallback. Tradeoffs?
sam (ux): From an end-user POV, gaps are super noisy. Dual-accept server-side + short canary seems lowest friction. Users won't need any action.
sara (eng-platform): Agree. Also we should avoid creating too many transient route ids in the console. If SDK starts sending both, some dashboards will split metrics (same route, two keys).
linh (eng): Good point. If clients send both headers we need to ensure ingestion collapses to canonical id (prefer new header value). We can add a normalization step in the telemetry mapper.
dmitri (eng-runtime): Implementation sketch (in ingestion):
```
# pseudocode
route = headers.get('X-RW-Policy') or headers.get('X-Redwood-Policy')
canonical = normalize_route(route)
emit_metric(route_id=canonical, ...)
```
kevin (devex): For SDKs: we could default to the new header but ship an opt-in compat flag `send_legacy_policy_header=true` so integrators can enable both during rollout. Default false to avoid duplicate traffic by default.
linh (eng): Would prefer server-side dual-accept for 14 days + a 10% canary that only sends new header from clients. Then update SDKs to new default in next minor release.
sam (ux): FYI, console tile needs continuity for the week of the release. Can we schedule the migration for a Tuesday morning?
dmitri (eng-runtime): Ops-bot: schedule canary window?
ops-bot: @dmitri scheduled canary on Tue 03:00 UTC, duration 48h, 10% ramp. Link: https://deploys/redwood/canary/5077
kevin (devex): SDK work: I'll open PRs for py/ts to add opt-in flag + config example. Sample Python snippet for docs: 
```
from redwood import Client
c = Client(...)
c.headers['X-RW-Policy'] = 'route:my-feature'
# optional for migration
# c.headers['X-Redwood-Policy'] = 'route:my-feature'  # set if send_legacy_policy_header=true
```
sara (eng-platform): Docs note: add migration FAQ explaining why header changed and how console maps both.
linh (eng): Telemetry sampling note: because we do 1% high-frequency sampling on heatmaps, make sure the normalization runs before sampling decision or we'll undercount.
dmitri (eng-runtime): Good catch — normalize first, sample second. I'll add tests.
kevin (devex): Action items: 1) @dmitri add dual-accept + normalization in ingestion (due Fri), 2) @kevin open SDK PRs with `send_legacy_policy_header` flag + canary docs (due Thu), 3) @sam add console continuity test for tile during canary (due Mon).
sara (eng-platform): sgtm. If anything slips we revert mapping change server-side. :thumbsup:
kevin (devex): I'll tag the PRs with migration:policy-header and include the ops canary link.
linh (eng): one more: bump telemetry ingestion log level during canary so we can trace unmatched headers without sampling overload.
dmitri (eng-runtime): Will do.
sam (ux): Thanks all — agree on Tue canary. I'll coordinate notification to support and CS.
sara (eng-platform): closing loop: we'll keep both headers accepted for 14 days then remove legacy header acceptance if metrics look good.
kevin (devex): perfect. I'll post a short blurb in #announcements the day before.
